canonicalExplanation.summary: A **package** (`package com.shop.billing;`) gives classes a full name and forms an **access boundary**. Java has four access levels. **public**: anyone. **protected**: the same package, plus subclasses in other packages (through inheritance). **package-private** (no keyword): **every class in the same package**, not just the same file. **private**: only inside the same top-level class. Good design exposes a **small public surface**, usually an interface and a factory, and keeps implementation classes package-private so callers **can't depend on details** you might change. Every public type and member is a promise you'll have to keep.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
A learner makes every class and method public "so nothing breaks". Six months later they want to replace their StripeGateway class, but three other packages construct it directly and call its helper methods. They also believe a method with no modifier is private to its file. Implementation classes remain package-private behind one public service interface, reducing the surface callers can couple to. In this lesson you'll create a coherent package structure and justify each exposed type or member.


examples.title: One public interface, hidden implementations
examples.situation: Implementation classes remain package-private behind one public service interface, reducing the surface callers can couple to.
walkthrough: **Implementation classes remain package-private:** CardPayments and Ledger have no modifier.
**Behind one public service interface:** callers use Payments and Payments.create().
**Reducing the surface callers can couple to:** we can replace CardPayments without changing any other package.
examples.result: The billing package can change freely inside its boundary.

examples.title: The gateway everyone depended on
examples.situation: Three packages call new StripeGateway() and its public helper methods, so replacing it means editing all of them.
walkthrough: The class and its helpers were public without a reason.
Introduce a public Payments interface and a factory.
Make the gateway and helpers package-private and migrate callers once.
examples.result: Future replacements touch only the billing package.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: Package-private members are private to one source file, and protected means accessible only by subclasses everywhere.
misconceptions.correction: Package-private means the whole package can access a member, and protected adds subclass access on top of package access.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In the opening predict, who could call the method with no modifier?

analogy.example: A package is like **an office floor**. **Private** is your desk drawer. **Package-private** is the shared kitchen: anyone on the floor can use it. **Protected** is the kitchen plus family members visiting from other floors. **Public** is the front reception desk, and everything there is something you've promised visitors.
limitations: Moving something from reception back to the kitchen upsets visitors.
Factories are the receptionist fetching staff for you.

steps.explanation: One public service interface is the only surface callers can couple to.
Implementation classes remain package-private behind the interface.
Outside code can't depend on hidden implementation details.

trace.textAlternative: Tracing access boundaries. Step 1, Expose: visible to Main is Payments, create, charge. One public service interface is the only surface callers can couple to. Step 2, Hide: CardPayments is package-private; ledger field is private. Implementation classes remain package-private behind the interface. Step 3, Reject: result is compile error: not public. Outside code can't depend on hidden implementation details.

Record why each public is needed.

remediation.explanation: For each type and member ask: **who outside this package truly needs it?** If nobody, drop the modifier. If only subclasses, consider protected.
remediation.retryPrompt: Apply this to "The gateway everyone depended on".

recap.summary: To create a coherent package structure and justify each exposed type or member, group related classes in a package, keep implementations package-private and fields private, expose a small public interface with a factory, and widen access only for a real caller.
